title: Clarinet
summary: A published 1981 Buffet Crampon Prestige bore and tone-hole lattice, blown at the published mezzo-forte mouth pressure with a lumped reed of published mass, stiffness and damping, observed at the physical baffled outlet receiver. Of the 21 fingerings of the committed chart (all rendered; Gb3, Gb5 and F6 have no chart row, being outside the cumulative open set), the all-holes-closed D3 and the register-hole note Bb4 speak a clean harmonic series at their pitch; Eb3 (lowest hole open) and A4 (register hole only) speak but carry a line near 1.1 kHz that is stronger than their fundamental; F3 speaks only when the mouth pressure rises in 15 ms or faster; the other 16 (G3, Ab3, Bb3, C4, D4, Eb4, F4, Gb4, G4, C5, D5, Eb5, F5, G5, A5, Bb5) fall into a parasitic regime between 0.8 and 2.6 kHz instead of their fundamental, and an abrupt start changes none of them. An offline linear-threshold prediction made before the last six renders (rule fixed in advance: the sounding maximum against the best competing maximum, speaks if the margin ratio is 0.9 or less, parasitic at 1.1 or more) called 16 of the 18 decisive fingerings right and missed F3 (attack) and G3 (ratio 0.88, parasitic on either start, while Bb4 at the same 0.88 speaks); its three undecided fingerings (Ab3 0.96, Eb4 1.08, C5 1.04) all render parasitic, so between about 0.75 and 1.05 the ratio does not decide. The same failure occurs for the published reed at its own published pressure. Graded by the P2 tool against the UIowa clarinet recordings (pairs regraded at 05:14Z; a measure is inside when its gap does not exceed the real-vs-real ruler, the strict ruler in brackets, one measure of D3, A4 and Bb4 has no ruler): D3 is inside on 9 of 15 measures (8), Eb3 on 9 (7), A4 on 4 (2), Bb4 on 3 (3). Bb4 was first refused because of the reference recording's very steep onset (a 40 dB rise in about 100 ms), not because of the render, and was graded after P2's steady-level onset rule. All of them are much brighter than the recordings, have no breath noise floor, and carry a start-up transient from the bore's priming wave. Diagnostic renders (not landed) that changed only the reed damping ratio did not find the cause: the published 0.0765 and the in-mouth model value 0.2 (q_r 0.4 of Silva, Kergomard, Vergez and Gilbert 2008, arXiv 0810.2870) do not make F3 or G3 speak, 0.3 does, and at 1.0, which is critical damping and not a cited value, F3 to D4 speak while D5 and A5 still do not. Diagnostic renders (not landed) of F3, Ab3, C4, D4, Gb4, D5 and A5 at damping ratio 0.2 changed one more property at a time and found no cited value that separates speaking from parasitic: the committed 3.1 kHz reed, the reed resonances 1883, 2368 and 3687 Hz (Gaillard, Koehl and Gazengel 2024, Acta Acustica 8, 63, Table A7, reed plus lip) and 1500 Hz (just under the 1530 to 1890 Hz of a wet reed on a mouthpiece, Table A6) and a 1.04 cm3 reed equivalent volume (the UNSW clarinet impedance page) leave all seven parasitic. Values outside every cited range do separate them, each only for some notes: a reed resonance of 500 Hz (about 40 times the committed reed mass) lets F3 to D4 speak, 750 Hz lets C4 to Gb4 speak, 1000 Hz lets Gb4 and D5 speak, all flat by up to 55 cents, and A5 never speaks; 4 cm3 of extra input volume lets F3 and Ab3 speak about 110 and 125 cents flat. An offline finite-element check (not landed) of the reed on its lay under the lip, built from the measured reed thickness, lay profile and lip stiffness of Avanzini and van Walstijn 2004 (Acta Acustica 90, Table I, Eqs. 18 and 19; the lip height solved to give their 0.4 mm rest opening; it reproduces their 1.4 kHz reed alone), does not lower the effective reed resonance in the mouth: 1.4 kHz for the reed alone, 1.75 kHz pressed on the lay at rest, and 3.1 to 3.5 kHz at the mezzo-forte blowing pressure, where only 7 to 8 mm of the tip is free and the damping ratio is 0.008. Three lumped equivalents of that state rendered through the engine leave the seven fingerings parasitic, except F3 in one of them, and one equivalent does not oscillate at all. The passive bore was also compared with measured clarinet input impedance (UNSW, Dickens, France, Smith and Wolfe, a Yamaha Custom CX Bb clarinet, reed compliance excluded, 118 to 4002 Hz; published facts, no licence stated, only scalars kept): for F3, C4, D4 and Gb4 (written G3, D4, E4, G#4) the strongest 0.8 to 2.6 kHz maximum is 6.0, 6.5, 4.4 and 3.1 dB under the sounding maximum, against 4.0, 2.5, 2.1 and 1.1 dB in fs-duct, which is also 2 to 4 dB too high at the sounding maximum and 4 to 7 dB too high at the 0.8 to 2.6 kHz maximum in absolute impedance. A real clarinet therefore also has strong upper maxima and still plays its fundamental. A diagnostic offline surrogate (a lumped reed on the same plane-wave bore, not the engine; it reproduces the engine's baseline failure of all seven fingerings and 7 of 8 of its reed damping and resonance checks) with the viscothermal loss raised by a factor 2 (f / 1 kHz) to the power 0.25, calibrated to the measured impedance heights only and not landed, lets F3 and Ab3 speak their fundamental and leaves C4, D4, Gb4, D5 and A5 parasitic; C4 and D4 need between 1.5 and 2 times that loss, and Gb4, D5 and A5 still do not speak at 2 times. The measured instrument is not the modelled one. Of the cited tone-hole loss terms fs-duct lacks only the edge viscous term of Keefe 1982, 0.25 k d_v ln(2b/r_c) (Keefe's viscous and radiation terms are otherwise present, the radiation twice as large because fs-duct's hole is flanged); sized with the plane-wave check it removes 0.2 to 0.6 dB of the 5.7 dB excess at the 0.8 to 2.6 kHz maxima even for a very sharp edge (r_c between 1 mm and 0.02 mm), and the open-hole radiation resistance would have to be about ten times the flanged value to reach the measured heights, which no cited mechanism supplies; the chimney edge radius, pad height and undercuts of the Buffet are UNKNOWN. The cause is open. The specimen is a population proxy for the UIowa R13, not the same instrument.
physics_present: fs-duct transfer-matrix air column built from the published Taillard and Sanchez 2016 bore station table, split at every chimney and never decimated, with the Vandoren M30 exit cone
every tone hole as a side branch (published position, minimal diameter and chimney height) with a flanged open mouth; the Moers and Kergomard 2011 normal-set chart decides which are open
flanged radiation load at the bell and the physical baffled outlet receiver (32 rings x 128 angles, 4.8 kHz band) for the radiated pressure, not the listener_m proxy

lumped single reed with mass, stiffness and damping, from the published Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2009 set (mass per area, effective area, stiffness per area, damping rate), so the reed has a resonance near 2.5 to 3 kHz; the closing pressure per note follows a declared lip-force rule
mezzo-forte mouth pressure interpolated from Fuks and Sundberg 1996 (two professionals on a Buffet Crampon Prestige), applied after a rest and held

shared woodwind exhaled-breath gas pack breath-woodwind-exhaled-coltman1966-nederveen1969 (27 C, 101325 Pa, RH 1.0, 4.5 percent dry CO2, 16.5 percent dry O2; Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969/1998, Fletcher and Rossing 1998)
physics_missing: fingerings with two or more lower tone holes open do not speak: the oscillator leaves the fundamental for a bore resonance between 0.8 and 2.6 kHz, and the extra lines of the Eb3 and A4 renders (1085 and 1135 Hz) lie on passive impedance maxima found by an independent plane-wave check, so the line is a real resonance of the modelled bore that the reed regenerates. Reed damping is a lever but not the cause: with the other inputs unchanged F3 and G3 speak at damping ratio 0.3 and 1.0 and not at 0.0765, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20 or (F3) 0.25; at 0.3 F5 also speaks while Ab3, C4, D4, Gb4, D5 and A5 do not; at 1.0 Ab3, C4, D4 and Gb4 speak and D5 and A5 do not. Not yet separated: how several open holes combine in the bore (the fs-duct |Z_in| of every chart fingering agrees with an independent plane-wave check to about 2.3 dB, so the bore model is not the defect; both share the flanged-chimney idealisation), the reed closure, the reed resonance and mass loading in the mouth (a mass-controlled reed at 0.8 to 2.6 kHz suppresses the parasitic line but needs a resonance below every cited value, and no single value serves all notes), hole geometry without undercuts, and the equivalent-cylinder mouthpiece

too bright and too clean: the reed closes against the lay with one very hard contact constant and no lay curvature, so it shuts abruptly and the high partials stay strong; there is no breath or turbulence noise, and the bore's 5 Pa priming wave leaves a start-up transient before the attack. The brightness is reed closure: Bb4's flat plateau of harmonics 8 to 14 at -33 dB under the fundamental is absent at 0.49 of the closing pressure and present at 0.52 (and the committed A4 is a clean 440 Hz series at 0.44 to 0.45, then a second oscillation at 695 Hz with 1135 Hz as its sum with the fundamental switches on between 0.45 and 0.46 and lifts the level four times; the measured UNSW impedance of written B4 has the same 5th-to-3rd maximum height ratio as the model, so the bore is not the cause). The engine's lay is a power law of 1.3e5 N/m2 that starts only at closure, 60 to 500 times softer than the cited clarinet lays. The reed row can now carry a measured lay (stiffness, exponent, onset opening, Hunt-Crossley loss; a six-field row is unchanged). Tested on 2026-10-21 with the Pamies-Vila 2021 Fig 6.5 medians (7.9e6 N/m2, exponent 2, onset 0.20 mm, loss 6.47 s/m): on the authored reed it removes A4's two-tone state (partial-frequency gap 13.5 to 1.3 of the strict ruler) but lowers the strict count from 20 to 17 of 57 (D3 8, Eb3 5, A4 3, Bb4 1), because the mean opening under 4 kPa then sits at the onset and the attack and the level change; the whole median set (reed and lay, committed area and width) leaves A4 and Bb4 silent and scores 11. Nothing was adopted: the committed renders and the 20 stand. Amplitude-dependent register-hole loss, which the engine's linear bore cannot carry, and the lip-force rule remain the open levers for A4

the reed set is a published model parameter set, not a measurement of the Vandoren reed and B40 or James Canter mouthpieces the players used; the effective area S_r is a corrected misprint (printed 7.61e5 m2, read as 7.61e-5 m2) and the damping unit is read as a rate; lip force is a rule, not a measurement; the damping of a reed held by a lip is UNKNOWN (route: artificial-mouth reed and lip impedance tables), and neither the cited reed+lip damping factors (0.03 to 0.24) and resonances (1883 to 3687 Hz) of Gaillard, Koehl and Gazengel 2024, Table A7, nor the in-mouth model value 0.2, make the open-hole fingerings speak; the committed set is a lumped fit to a simulated reed with lips and lay (DAFx-09 section 2), not an in-vivo measurement, and the lip-force rule raises its stiffness 2.2 times above the paper's own, so the committed reed resonates at 3.0 to 3.1 kHz with damping ratio 0.077 to 0.080 where the paper's set gives 2.1 kHz and 0.114; a plus or minus 15 percent change of that resonance moves the parasitic line of C4, D4 and Gb4 by at most 0.5 percent (F3 hops to another passive maximum), so the line is a bore maximum pulled 3 to 5 percent flat and the reed decides only which maximum wins; the estimate from a clarinettist's mouthpiece signals in Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012 (Table 2, read in the authors' manuscript: stiffness 2195 N/m, mass 9.9e-6 kg, resonance 2368 Hz, damping ratio 0.015, closing pressure 3162 Pa, blowing pressure 1671 Pa, one note on a simplified bore) is lighter damped than ours, and heavy damping with a low resonance (672 Hz, quality factor 1.13) is reported only for a tenor saxophone reed (Munoz Arancon et al. 2016, read from the review table only: its HAL record holds no file). Rendered with their own blowing pressures, neither the paper's theoretical set (resonance 2095 Hz, damping ratio 0.114, 1800 Pa) nor that player estimate keeps the committed speaking map: D3 and A4 speak but Eb3 and Bb4 do not, and F3, C4, D4 and Gb4 stay parasitic on bore maxima of 0.75 to 1.0 kHz or higher; with the Fuks and Sundberg blowing pressures (3.3 to 4.0 kPa) and the paper's own stiffness the reed is shut (closing pressure 3464 Pa) and the engine refuses the closed-hole notes. The committed lip-force rule, which scales the stiffness so the Fuks blowing pressure sits at the paper's operating ratio of 0.52, is therefore what makes four notes speak, and it is authored and UNKNOWN as a physical quantity. Lip-loaded sources searched on 2026-10-21: the only direct measurement of a reed under an artificial lip found is Gazengel, Guimezanes, Dalmont et al., ISMA 2007 (cane reed on a mouthpiece, loudspeaker excitation, abstract only, HAL hal-03179547): two modes, the first highly damped near 1200 Hz and the second near 4000 Hz at high lip pressure; its damping, stiffness, mass, area, lip pressure and instrument are UNKNOWN, so it cannot be a reed record. The nearest clarinet sets are inverse-model estimates from a player: Pamies-Vila 2021 thesis Fig. 6.5 (per-tone medians over 11 clarion tones of one Bb clarinet excerpt, embouchure included: mass 1.68 mg, damping rate 2270.54 1/s, stiffness 1434.15 N/m, opening 0.36 mm, from which resonance 4650 Hz and damping ratio 0.039; area and width not printed) and the 2012 estimate above; Worman 1971 (3687 Hz, damping ratio 0.063, via the review table) is an isolated-reed measurement and the 2007 van Walstijn and Avanzini range is a simulation. The linear-threshold prediction over all 21 fingerings with each cited set (bead comment 2026-10-21) makes at most 7 fingerings speak (the Pamies-Vila medians, with 9 more undecided at parity; the committed reed gives 6) and shuts the reed at the Fuks and Sundberg pressures for every set whose closing pressure lies below them, so no cited lip-loaded set replaces the authored rule, which stays UNKNOWN
the mouthpiece chamber, baffle, throat and lay are unknown; the cavity is an equivalent cylinder matched to the published internal volume and length
open tone holes do not radiate in the observer (only the bell does), and undercuts, pad geometry and key rise are unknown

passive bore loss is too low: against the measured Yamaha Custom CX of UNSW the modelled sounding maxima are 1.5 to 5 dB too high (mean 2.9 dB over 15 fingerings) and the 0.8 to 2.6 kHz maxima 4 to 7 dB too high for the open-hole fingerings, so the missing loss grows with frequency; an independent plane-wave check shows that raising the viscothermal loss uniformly closes the sounding maximum at about 1.4 times, the upper maxima at 1.8 to 3 times, and not the gap between them. Pads over open holes, undercuts, wall roughness and hole radiation are the candidate mechanisms; their parameters are UNKNOWN for the Buffet Prestige and none is in fs-duct. The measured instrument is a different clarinet from the modelled one

the reed is a single lumped oscillator on one slit lay: the reed rolling onto the curved lay under the lip (a stiffening static law with a closing pressure near 20 kPa and a mean opening of only 0.05 to 0.08 mm at mezzo-forte for the reed of Avanzini and van Walstijn 2004) and the lip's own mass and damping are not simulated in the engine, only linearised offline; the cited lip height and Young's modulus of that paper were fine-tuned by its authors, and the effect of the contact dynamics within a cycle is not tested

no amplitude-dependent hole loss: at playing level open tone holes shed vortices and add a resistance proportional to the acoustic velocity in the hole, which fs-duct and the regional line do not have and the low-level UNSW impedance cannot show; the sharp-edge coefficients read in Szwarcberg et al. 2024 from Dalmont et al. 2002 are series 0.4 Z_c v / c and shunt (0.5 Z_ch + 0.1 Z_c) v / c, and Atig et al. 2004 show the edge radius of curvature decides (onset near 10 m/s at 4 mm, below 0.5 m/s for a sharp edge), the Buffet's being UNKNOWN; the offline surrogate with the sharp-edge values at a frozen 2 to 10 m/s in every open hole (open-hole velocities of 1 to 7 mm/s per Pa RMS at the mouthpiece, similar for the parasitic line and the fundamental) leaves F3, C4, D4 and Gb4 parasitic on the same lines because the resistance lowers the fundamental's impedance peak at least as much as the upper maxima; Szwarcberg et al. report that a linear-impedance model never produces the second register on their test resonators while nonlinear loss in the register hole does; applied to the register hole only in the offline surrogate it lowers the first-register impedance peak from -4.8 to -10 dB re the largest at 10 m/s as they describe, but that surrogate does not reproduce the engine's A4 (clean there, strong 1.1 kHz line in the engine) or Bb4 (parasitic there, clean in the engine), so the test cannot be read for those two notes

terms of the linearised reed-bore loop that rise with frequency (offline, committed reed, C4, D4, Gb4): the reed-opening feedback through the reed response 1 / (k - m w^2 + j w r) rises 19, 23 and 13 percent from the sounding to the parasitic frequency, set by the stiffness (the authored lip-force rule, resonance 3.0 kHz against 2.1 kHz in the paper's own set), the mass and damping (cited), and holding it at its static value turns the parasitic-to-sounding margin ratio 1.15, 1.17, 1.18 into 0.89, 0.88, 0.99, so it is the dominant term; the swept-flow term A h' grows with frequency but A is the cited effective area S_r (7.61e-5 m2; the 2012 paper's own Table 1 prints 7.62e-5, confirming the misprint reading) and the term is mostly reactive (it pulls the regime 3 to 5 percent flat) with a loss part that lowers the parasitic margin by 6 to 10 percent, so scaling it by 0 to 2 changes the ratio by at most about 10 percent; no flow inertance of the reed channel and no mouth or vocal-tract impedance are in the loop (UNKNOWN); the mouthpiece volume (11.2 cm3 cited, equivalent shape authored) acts through the bore impedance; with the measured passive-loss deficit the linear ratio becomes 0.87 to 0.90, yet the surrogate in time still ends parasitic for C4 at that loss (it needs twice as much), so the linear ratio alone does not decide the regime

the attack is a mouth-pressure ramp and the performance format has no tongue or lip-force track: F3 ends on its fundamental when the pressure rises in 15 ms or faster (a reed pre-closed by pressure above the closing pressure gives the identical result) and parasitic at 1178 Hz when it rises in 20 ms or slower, whatever the control clock, so the committed 20 ms attack (authored, UNKNOWN) sits just past the switch; C4, D4, Gb4, Ab3, D5 and A5 end parasitic for every start tried. Offline linear thresholds of the committed reed on the bore explain the split: for C4, D4 and Gb4 the 1.1 to 1.4 kHz maximum has the lowest oscillation threshold (0.35 of the closing pressure against 0.37 to 0.38) and the larger growth margin (3.9 to 4.8 against 3.4 to 4.0), while for F3 the fundamental has the lowest threshold (0.40) and the larger margin (2.68 against 2.02) and is lost only in the transient; with the reed resonance below 1 kHz the parasitic margin is negative and with a stiff reed (6 to 8 kHz) the two margins are within 10 percent, so the outcome rests on small differences. A measured tongue release is not available: Pamies-Vila, Hofmann and Chatziioannou 2018 (Frontiers in Psychology, ten players, synthetic reed) report tongue contact of 37 ms (SD 14) in portato, mean mouth pressure 2.7 kPa piano and 3.8 to 4.2 kPa forte, and mouthpiece-pressure attack times of 29 to 48 ms, but no release speed and no reed displacement at release. Li, Almeida, Smith and Wolfe 2016 (J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 139, 825 with clarinettists; 140, 1089 with a playing machine) show that players raise the mouth pressure while the tongue holds the reed and release it at or near the playing pressure, below or above the oscillation threshold (above it more often for accented low notes; a minimal attack rises at only 1.2 to 1.6 kPa/s), and the machine study names the flow pulse from the changing aperture after release as the starting mechanism (tongue force 0.05 to 0.15 N, initial reed displacement about 0.2 mm): a ramp from zero against an open reed is therefore not a measured gesture, no measured mouth-pressure rise time exists to set it from, the committed 20 ms stays UNKNOWN, and both starts are reported (20 ms ramp: F3 parasitic; pre-closed release or any rise of 15 ms or faster: F3 fundamental)

one ambient gas serves both the bore and the room: the bore uses the shared woodwind exhaled-breath pack breath-woodwind-exhaled-coltman1966-nederveen1969 (27 C, 101325 Pa, RH 1.0, 4.5 percent dry CO2, 16.5 percent dry O2; Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969/1998, Fletcher and Rossing 1998), and RegionalDuct::with_exterior_gas refuses a separate room-air exterior on the 20 fingerings with open or vented tone holes because fs-duct's combined chimney-and-radiation law takes a single medium ('an exposed tone hole with a different exterior gas needs an unavailable two-medium chimney law'). Consequently the baffled-outlet observer also runs in the breath mixture under the classical Stokes-Kirchhoff attenuation law (ISO 9613-1 is calibrated for atmospheric dry air and rejects non-atmospheric CO2/O2 mole fractions). The size of this single-gas limitation is small: at the bell and open holes, rho*c in the breath mixture (1.1709 kg/m3, 345.36 m/s, 404.38 Pa s/m) is 1.9 to 2.2 percent (0.17 to 0.19 dB) lower than in 20 C room air (412.2 to 413.3 Pa s/m for RH 50 to 0 percent), and over the 0.5 m listener distance the Stokes-Kirchhoff absorption in breath (0.0007 dB at 1 kHz, 0.017 dB at 4.8 kHz) differs from ISO 9613-1 absorption in 20 C room air (0.0025 to 0.0030 dB at 1 kHz, 0.018 to 0.035 dB at 4.8 kHz for RH 20 to 50 percent) by at most 0.002 dB at 1 kHz and 0.019 dB at 4.8 kHz; on the all-holes-closed D3 (where with_exterior_gas is admitted), adding exterior 293.15 101325 0 with ISO 9613-1 shifts f0 by -0.1 cents (145.88 Hz) and raises the radiated RMS pressure at 0.5 m by +0.180 dB (0.4963 to 0.5062 Pa)
no wall vibration, no player airway, lips or tongue, no vibrato; the lumped reed has one mode and no reed continuum
the specimen is not the UIowa Buffet R13 and no same-specimen passive comparison exists yet; fingerings outside the normal set have no chart
